chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fazzal, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad Al-Ash'ari, from Aban ibn Abdul Malik, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said:
Do not express gloating to your brother, for Allah may be Merciful to him and Make it come with you.
And he said: The one who gloats over a difficulty which descends upon his brother, would not exit from the world until he is Tried with it.

key_terms.الشَّمَاتَةَ: Gloating or rejoicing in another's misfortune
key_terms.يُفْتَنَ: To be tried or tested (with a similar affliction)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual consequence of gloating over a Muslim's misfortune?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) warns against *al-shamat* (gloating), a subtle spiritual disease that corrupts the heart and invites divine retribution. He emphasizes that Allah may reciprocate the gloater's joy by turning the specific trial upon them, ensuring that no one escapes this fate without experiencing a similar affliction. This teaching underscores the Shia emphasis on *mu'akhat* (brotherhood) and emotional empathy as essential components of faith.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Bin Fazzal, from Ibrahim Bin Muhammad Al Ashary, from Aban Bin Abdul Malik, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Do not express the gloating to your brother, for Allah<sup>azwj</sup> could be Merciful to him and Make it to come with you’.
And he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The one who gloats (rejoices) over a difficulty which descends upon his brother, would not exit from the world until he is (also) Tried with it’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from al-Hassan ibn Ali ibn Faddal from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Ash’ari from Aban ibn ‘Abd al-Malik from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, ‘
Do not express joy at the trouble of your brother (in belief); Allah may grant him a favor and transfer that trouble to you.’
The Imam also said, ‘Whoever rejoices at the suffering that has come upon his brother (in belief) he will not leave this world before going through such suffering himself.’”
